recipes.name: Teriyaki Shiitake Shoyu Ramen
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Cook the garlic, ginger, doubanjiang, shiitake, and enoki for 1 minute.
Add the bouillon, water, soy sauce, and kombu. Bring to a boil, lower to a simmer, covered with a lid and cook for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, drizzle the sesame oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. When hot, add the corn and salt. Cook until golden, then transfer to a plate.
Heat some more oil in the now-empty pan. Cook the shiitake mushrooms until golden.
Turn off the heat and add the teriyaki sauce to the mushrooms. Stir to coat.
Cook the noodles according to the package instructions. When cooked, remove the noodles from the water, but don't discard the water yet. Toss the noodles in a bit of toasted sesame oil.
Bring the noodle water back to a boil and add the bok choy. Cook for 30 - 60 seconds before draining.
When the broth is ready, remove the kombu. Add the sugar, vinegar, and sesame oil to the broth and stir through.
Add the noodles to a bowl, pour over the broth, and top with corn, teriyaki mushrooms, and other desired toppings. Enjoy!

page_recipe_notes: Notes † Kombu, or dried kelp, is used to add a savoury umami flavour to soups and stews, especially in Japanese dishes. It can be found in Asian grocery stores. Avoid substituting it with nori sheets, as they have a different texture and flavour profile. † Traditionally, teriyaki sauce is made with just soy sauce, sake (or mirin), and sugar. Make sure to check the ingredients of your bottle so it doesn't have too many other ingredients that may affect the flavour.

Storage This soup is best enjoyed immediately. The broth can be made a day in advance and stored in an airtight container in the fridge for up to 4 days. Reheat on the stove before adding the toppings and noodles.
